I find it really hard to put a minus number on the forecast, but you're clearly many hundreds of millions ahead of the three-year plan in [Global Markets]. So, I wonder whether you'd share a view on whether anything we've seen in the outperformance so far is structural. And then secondly, I wonder whether you'd give us a perspective on what you're hearing from shareholders on the increased cost plans. Clearly a hundred percent RoI is better than we can do in most organic businesses, but if the bank can't deliver outperformance in a bull market, what you're really doing is de-risking the same road here as we already have in our models. I just wonder whether shareholders are happy with that and how they're taking the near-term plans?",
  "answer_quote": "Okay. So let me start with the [Global Markets] business. So, it would be useful if you have a quick look at page 41 [of the Q2 results presentation]. Let me take a longer lens to this Jason. We have two objectives within revenue within the Investment Bank. The first is to grow the more stable sources of income on an absolute basis. And on the chart that I'm showing you on page 41, they are Financing and the International Corporate Bank, and you can see those growing over time. And one thing to think about would be, back to that point about operating leverage and the ability to generate a return in the Investment Bank, not just in a bull market, but in a market where there may be an air-pocket in opportunities. Think about the proportion of the IB costs that those stable revenues cover, because that's important. That's gone from about 50% to about 80%, and that means that as you are getting upside, either from fees because of the opportunity in Investment Banking, or from [Global Markets], the Intermediation line, then that has much more feeling on the P&L. The second thing we've been trying to do is to diversify our [Global Markets] effort, alongside areas that we feel are very strong for Barclays. So, whether it's Securitised Products within the FICC business or whether it's Equity Derivatives within Equities, growing alongside Prime. And what that does is it gives us chance to be more successful in the range of environments. So, if you look at that chart, it also makes the business less seasonal. What you are seeing is the peak to trough is narrowing. It's still there of course, this is a seasonal business, it's seasonal for everybody. You would expect it to be a bit more seasonal for us, given our stage of development. But we're trying to compress that H1 to H2 drop off. So a few years back, a performance like what we've just achieved in Q2 would not have been possible for Barclays, because we would not have had the Equities franchise to be able to deliver it. So, clearly we are benefiting from a market that is much bigger than we planned for, but we are in part monetizing that because of the structural things that we have put in place that underpin it. So, I think of it as making structural progress not just in revenue, but in our capital allocation discipline, in our cost discipline and that's what's really driving the RoTE to the bottom line. And even after the SCAs that we are calling out for this year, and even after the change in the MRT [costs], then, we are expecting this to hit circa 12% this year, which is good progress and continuing to build out that structural base. To your question on the perspective from shareholders, I think if we were thinking about a permanent and elevated level of investment, it would be a different topic. But what we are saying is, we can see opportunities to do some of the things that we were envisaging through our three-year plan, faster [and] quicker, not just because we have the upside, but because we have better line of sight as to what they are and better confidence in being able to deliver them and move on. That is a positive thing, in that it creates a longer-term progression for the RoTE and in so doing, what we are trying to do is balance the upside here, between a progression in the RoTE number, between a progression in the distribution, and the distributions were up 61% in the first half. So really ensuring that that money is in the hands of the shareholders and it's going back faster than they would've seen previously, because of the quarterly buyback and because of the way that we've now balanced the dividends. So certainly from the conversations that we've had, Jason, it is a balance of all of these things.",
